summary.name: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing SMTP, the Internet standard protocol used to send and relay electronic mail between mail servers and from mail clients to servers.
use_cases: understanding how email is transmitted between servers
configuring an email client's outgoing mail server
learning the history of email protocols
reviewing SMTP session commands and replies
summary.what_it_does: The page explains SMTP as a text-based, connection-oriented delivery protocol that runs over TCP and uses commands such as HELO/EHLO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO and DATA. It covers the mail processing model, from client submission through MX lookup and hand-off between MTAs to local delivery, with IMAP or POP used for retrieval. It describes historical development from RFC 772 and RFC 788 in 1981 through ESMTP (RFC 1869), SMTP-AUTH and submission ports, and includes a sample SMTP session transcript. It also discusses access control for outgoing servers, including IP-based restriction versus client authentication.
notable: Covers the history of SMTP from ARPANET-era predecessors to modern ESMTP extensions
Includes a step-by-step example SMTP session transcript
Explains the separation of mail submission (ports 587/465) from relay (port 25)
caveats: Original SMTP had no authentication or encryption and allowed open relaying, which led to spam problems
Many ISPs block outgoing port 25 traffic
